context.full_target:
The complete Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence), with its Section 2 standing definitions and fixed scheme, on PDF page 2.

Use the periodic domain mathbbT = reals/(2*pi*integers) with normalized measure dx/(2*pi). For a periodic function f, hat f(k) = (2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx and <k> = (1+k^2)^(1/2). The Sobolev norm is ||f||_(H^s)^2 = sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s) |hat f(k)|^2. These spaces are completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms, with negative-order spaces interpreted as distributions. Reality means hat f(-k) = conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0) = 0. Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms use essential suprema.

Let S_t = exp(-t*partial_x^3), with Fourier multiplier exp(i*t*k^3). Let P0 be the spatial mean and P = I-P0. Let D^(-1) = partial_x^(-1) have multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k != 0 and zero at k=0, and D^(-2) = (D^(-1))^2. The equation is
  u_t + u_xxx = (1/2)*partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u0.
The exact solution is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation.

For timestep tau=T/L, the time-semidiscrete scheme is exactly
  u^0 = u0,
  u^(n+1) = S_tau u^n + F_tau(u^n) + H_tau(u^n),
where all products below are spatial products and [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0):
  F_tau(f) = (1/6)*P[(S_tau D^(-1) f)^2]
             - (1/6)*S_tau P[(D^(-1) f)^2],
  H_tau(f) = (1/3)*P[(S_tau D^(-1) f)*D^(-1) F_tau(f)]
             + (tau/9)*(S_tau D^(-1) f)*P0(f^2)
             - (1/54)*[S_(tau-s) D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1) f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
             - (1/(27*tau))*[S_(tau-s) D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau) D^(-2) F_tau(f))*(S_s D^(-1) f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
This is the source scheme (2), with no spatial frequency cutoff.

For every T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0, there exist C>0 and tau0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(mathbbT) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, this fixed scheme satisfies
  max_(0<=n<=L) ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L^2) <= C*tau^gamma.
The constants are uniform over the entire stated initial-data ball and all permitted timesteps, with no Fourier-support restriction. The target includes all the hypotheses, quantifiers, endpoints, solution convention and method above.
context.conclusion: There exist C>0 and tau0>0, depending only on T,gamma,R, such that for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(mathbbT) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R, the unique distributional solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma) obtained by smooth approximation and the fixed unfiltered iterates of Psi satisfy max_(0<=n<=L)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_L2<=C*tau^gamma for every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0. The constants are uniform over that entire datum ball and all these L; no Fourier-support restriction is imposed.

record.definition: mathbbT=ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi).

For a periodic integrable f, hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx. The transform extends by completion to Sobolev spaces and by distributional duality. Reality means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

record.type: family of Fourier Sobolev spaces and norms
record.definition: For real s, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2), ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials, interpreted as distributions for negative s; L2=H^0 with the normalized spatial norm. On mean-zero functions ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Time suprema use continuous representatives and derivative norms essential suprema. For sequences x, ||x||_(ell2)^2=sum_k |x(k)|^2; ell1 uses sum_k |x(k)|. Frequency projections P_{<=A}, P_{>A} retain respectively |k|<=A and |k|>A.
S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k), for every real t.
P0 f=hat f(0), identified with the constant function.
P=I-P0.
Dinv=D^(-1)=partial_x^(-1): its multiplier is (i*k)^(-1) at k!=0 and zero at k=0. D^(-2)=Dinv composed with Dinv. Spatial derivatives use multiplier i*k.
For tau>0 and periodic f in L2, F_tau(f)=(1/6)*P[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)*S_tau P[(Dinv f)^2].

For tau>0 and periodic f in L2, H_tau(f)=(1/3)*P[(S_tau Dinv f)*Dinv F_tau(f)]+(tau/9)*(S_tau Dinv f)*P0(f^2)-(1/54)*[S_(tau-s) Dinv[(S_s Dinv f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)-(1/(27*tau))*[S_(tau-s) D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau) D^(-2) F_tau(f))*(S_s Dinv f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau). Every product is spatial and [G(s)]_0^tau=G(tau)-G(0).

record.type: unfiltered time-step map and its iterates
record.definition: Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+F_tau(f)+H_tau(f). For positive integer L set tau=T/L and t_n=n*tau. Define u^0=u0 and u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n) for 0<=n<L. There is no spatial cutoff in this recurrence.
For tau>0, M_tau g=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s)ds and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).

For tau>0, t_n=n*tau and k!=0, hat(R2_(n,tau)(f1,f2,f3))(k)= -tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t_n*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f1(a)*hat f2(b)*hat f3(c), with p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. Output at k=0 is zero. Initially this formula is on Fourier polynomials; bounded extension is proved below. Terms with a zero input frequency vanish since one phase is zero.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)].
J_t(f,g)=S_(-t) P[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].
For I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b, Cint_I(f,g,h)=integral_I S_(-t) P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))}dt; time-independent inputs are read as constant paths.
p_star=23/14. For an interval I of length at most one, ||f||_X(I)=||f||_(L^infty(I;L2))+||partial_t f||_(L^infty(I;H^(-p_star))).

record.definition: For 0<gamma<=1, a_gamma=1/2-gamma if gamma<1/2; a_gamma=1/8 if gamma=1/2; and a_gamma=0 if gamma>1/2.

For tau>0, nonnegative integer n, t_n=n*tau and t in [t_n,t_n+tau], Stage_(n,tau)(t;f)= (1/2) integral_(t_n)^t B_s(f,f)ds, initially for a time-independent smooth mean-zero f; the endpoint normal form below gives its L2 extension.

For smooth mean-zero step data f at t_n=n*tau, write F_n(t)=Stage_(n,tau)(t;f), z_n=f+F_n, C_n(t)=integral_(t_n)^t B_s(f,F_n(s))ds, Q_n(t)=(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(F_n(s),F_n(s))ds, W_n=Q_n(t_n+tau)+R2_(n,tau)(f,f,f), V_n(t)=f+F_n(t)+C_n(t)+Q_n(t)-(t-t_n)*W_n/tau, Y_n=V_n-z_n, rho_n(t)=-integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,z_n)ds-(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,Y_n)ds-(t-t_n)*W_n/tau. For f=S_(-t_n)u^n, concatenate V_n as V and the increments rho_n as Rres, with Rres(0)=0. Continuity of V at grid points is a proved property, not an assumption.

record.type: normalized periodic KdV equation and exact-solution convention
record.definition: KdV is the equation u_t+partial_x^3 u=(1/2)*partial_x(u^2) on mathbbT. For a real mean-zero datum q in H^s, s>=0, and horizon A>0, an exact solution u with datum q means the real mean-zero C([0,A];H^s) distributional solution of this equation with u(0)=q obtained by smooth approximation. An exact twisted solution v means v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) for this same equation and interval. A smooth exact solution means such a solution with smooth space and time dependence. These terms specify a solution relation only; existence, uniqueness, bounds and the differential equation for the twist are proved, rather than granted by this definition.

record.statement: For the real mean-zero 2*pi-periodic source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx, with normalized homogeneous norms, the following results hold in its norm-preserving twisted representation. For every s>=0, time horizon A>0 and L2 upper bound B0, Galerkin solutions with datum q in dot H^s and ||q||_2<=B0 obey sup_[0,A]||U_m||_(dot H^s)<=M_s, uniformly in m, with M_s depending only on s,A,B0,||q||_(dot H^s). For s>0 and 0<sigma<s, a subsequence converges strongly in L^p([0,A];H^sigma), 1<p<infinity, and weak-star in L^infty dot H^s to a distributional solution with the same bound and L2 conservation a.e.. This solution is unique, is C([0,A];dot H^s), preserves L2 at every time and depends Lipschitz continuously on the datum for s>1/2, and also for 0<s<=1/2. At s=0 there is a unique C([0,A];L2) solution with Lipschitz dependence obtained by smoothing. For theta in (-1,0] and two data q,r in L2 whose norms sum to at most B0, the two twisted flows satisfy sup_[0,A]||Utw-Vtw||_(dot H^theta)<=C' C_(B0)^A ||q-r||_(dot H^theta), where C',C_(B0) depend only on B0,theta.

Theorem 5.1. Let s >1/2, v(0) = v0 ∈ ˙H s, and let T > 0 be ﬁxed. Then the solution

source.statement: For Li-Wu's bilinear stage Stage_(n,tau)(t;f,g)=(1/2)integral_(n*tau)^t B_s(f,g)ds, for time-independent mean-zero f,g in H^sigma, sigma in (0,1], t in [n*tau,(n+1)*tau], one has ||Stage(t;f,g)||_(H^beta)<=C tau^((1+sigma-beta)/(1+sigma-beta0))||f||_(H^sigma)||g||_(H^sigma), for beta in [beta0,1+sigma]. Here beta0=2*sigma-3/2 for sigma<1/2; beta0=-1/2-epsilon with any fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0 for sigma=1/2; beta0=sigma-1 for sigma>1/2. Norms are the unnormalized source norms. The diagonal stage is Stage(t;f).

record.statement: For every smooth mean-zero f, tau>0 and nonnegative integer n, let t_n=n*tau and let q=S_(t_n)f. With the displayed Li-Wu maps F_tau,H_tau, its algebraic step identity is S_(-t_n-tau)[S_tau q+F_tau(q)+H_tau(q)]=f+Stage_(n,tau)(t_n+tau;f)+integral_(t_n)^(t_n+tau) B_s(f,Stage_(n,tau)(s;f))ds-R2_(n,tau)(f,f,f). The R2 has exactly the Fourier phase covariance, sign and coefficient of D012, including zero output.

source.statement: For every smooth mean-zero f, tau>0 and nonnegative integer n, let t_n=n*tau and let q=S_(t_n)f. With the displayed Li-Wu maps F_tau,H_tau, its algebraic step identity is S_(-t_n-tau)[S_tau q+F_tau(q)+H_tau(q)]=f+Stage_(n,tau)(t_n+tau;f)+integral_(t_n)^(t_n+tau) B_s(f,Stage_(n,tau)(s;f))ds-R2_(n,tau)(f,f,f). The R2 has exactly the Fourier phase covariance, sign and coefficient of D012, including zero output.

record.statement: For T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0 there is A=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity such that every real mean-zero datum q in H^gamma with ||q||_(H^gamma)<=R has a unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional solution u of u_t+u_xxx=u*u_x, obtained by smooth approximation, and sup_[0,T]||u||_(H^gamma)<=A. Smooth data give spatially smooth solutions on [0,T]. For two real mean-zero L2 data q,r of norms summing to at most B0, the exact solutions satisfy sup_[0,T]||u_q-u_r||_2<=C(T,B0)||q-r||_2. Twisting v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) preserves all Sobolev norms and for smooth data v'=B_t(v,v)/2. Consequently M=1+sup_[0,T]||v||_(H^gamma)<=1+A uniformly on the datum ball.

For every tau>0 and real alpha,beta, eta_tau=0 if either phase is zero. Otherwise |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=2 min(|alpha/beta|,|beta/alpha|) and |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=tau min(|alpha|,|beta|). For nonzero integers a,b,c,d with a+b+c+d=0 let N1>=N2>=N3>=N4 be the ordered absolute values, A=|ab| and B0=|cd|. Then N1<=3*N2, |d|^(-1)min(A/B0,B0/A)<=3/N3 and |a+b|/max(A,B0)<=6/N3.

record.statement: For arbitrary nonnegative x1,x2,x3,x4 in ell2(Z\{0}), sum_(a+b+c+d=0,abcd!=0) x1(a)x2(b)x3(c)x4(d)/N3(a,b,c,d)<=C product_(j=1)^4||x_j||_ell2, where N3 is the third largest of |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|. The same bound holds upon restricting the positive sum to any subset; C is absolute.

For every exponent s in [0,1], tau>0, nonnegative n and mean-zero f_j in H^s, R2_(n,tau) extends uniquely from polynomials to a trilinear map into L2 with ||R2_(n,tau)(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_s*tau^(1+s) product_j ||f_j||_(H^s), uniformly in n,tau and spectral support. The same estimate holds with any multiplier of modulus at most one in the defining sum, including separate restrictions to Phi=0 and Phi!=0. In particular, for 0<gamma<=1, ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M, f mean zero in L2, delta=||f-w||_2<=1 and 0<tau<=1, ||R2_(n,tau)(f,f,f)||_2<=C_(M,gamma)*tau*(tau^gamma+delta), with no H^gamma assumption on f.

record.statement: S_t is unitary in every H^s, preserves reality and zero mean. On mean-zero inputs, uniformly in real t: ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infty<=C||f||_2; ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-23/14))<=C||f||_2||g||_2; ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For every A0 in H^1, ||A0||_infty<=C||A0||_(H^1). For A0,B0 in H^1, ||A0 B0||_(H^1)<=C||A0||_(H^1)||B0||_(H^1). Also ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2, ||A0||_(H^(-23/14))<=||Dinv A0||_2 for mean-zero A0, and ||J_t(A0,B0)||_2<=C||Dinv A0||_2||B0||_2 whenever the right side is defined. For smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. Moreover J is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=Cint_I(f,g,h). These identities hold stepwise for piecewise smooth paths, and Stage_(n,tau)(t;f)=[J_s(f,f)]_(s=n*tau)^t/6.

record.statement: For 0<gamma<=1, a_gamma belongs to [0,1). In the normalized norms, for every interval I=[a,b] contained in [0,infinity) with |I|<=1 and L2 paths f1,f2,f3 with weak derivatives in L^infty(I;H^(-23/14)), ||Cint_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C|I| product_j||f_j||_X(I)+C||f_i||_(L^infty H^(-23/14)) product_(j!=i)||f_j||_(L^infty L2), for each i. For time-independent H^s inputs, 0<=s<=1, ||Cint_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_s |I|^s product_j||f_j||_(H^s). Furthermore ||fg||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^a_gamma). For every mean-zero w in H^gamma of norm <=M, 0<tau<=1 and n>=0, sup_step||Stage(t;w)||_(H^a_gamma)<=C_(M,gamma)tau^gamma and sup_step||Stage(t;w)||_(H^(1+gamma))<=C_(M,gamma). Constants are independent of interval position, step and spectral support.
record.origin: problem.md:334-369; source specialization and norm bridge

record.statement: For every smooth real mean-zero u0, tau>0 and finite number of steps, the iterates Psi_tau(u^n) remain smooth real and mean zero. With v^n=S_(-n*tau)u^n and Interp constructed from f=v^n, V is a continuous piecewise smooth path satisfying V(t_n)=v^n for every grid point, Y_n(t_n)=0, and on each step V'=B_t(V,V)/2+Rres', where Rres'=-B_t(Y_n,z_n)-B_t(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau. The concatenated Rres starts at zero and has increment rho_n on the step.
record.origin: problem.md:399-431,501-514; exact interpolation endpoints and residual identity

record.statement: For 0<gamma<=1, for every M>=1, smooth mean-zero f,w with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M and delta=||f-w||_2<=1, 0<tau<=1 and n>=0, set q=tau^gamma+delta and use the step tuple Interp(n,tau,f). Uniformly over its step: ||F_n||_(H^1)<=C_M, ||F_n-Stage(t;w)||_(H^1)<=C_M delta, ||F_n||_(H^a_gamma)+||F_n||_2<=C_M q, ||z_n||_X<=C_M, ||B_t(F_n,F_n)||_2<=C_M q, ||Q_n||_2+||W_n||_2<=C_M tau q, ||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_M tau q, ||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_M q, ||Y_n||_2<=C_M q, ||Y_n||_X<=C_M q and ||Y_n||_(H^(-23/14))<=C_M tau q. Constants may depend on M,gamma, never on n,tau or spectral support.

For 0<gamma<=1, every nonnegative integer n, M>=1, 0<tau<=1 and smooth mean-zero f,w with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M and delta=||f-w||_2<=1, set q=tau^gamma+delta. The step tuple Interp(n,tau,f) satisfies sup_step||rho_n||_2<=C_(M,gamma)*tau*q and ||Rres'||_(L^infty(step;H^(-23/14)))<=C_(M,gamma)*q, uniformly in n,tau and Fourier support.

For T>0 and 0<gamma<=1, let u be any smooth real mean-zero solution of u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)*partial_x(u^2) on [0,T], and set v(t)=S_(-t)u(t), so v is the exact twisted solution of the normalized KdV equation, with M=1+sup||v||_(H^gamma), and let V,Rres be the Interp paths of the fixed scheme initialized by v(0). Put e=v-V. For 0<tau<=1, every I=[a,b] subset [0,T] starting at a grid point, with h=b-a<=1 and E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1, satisfies for every real N>=2: E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_M(h+tau)tau^gamma+C_M(N^2 h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-23/14))E_I. The same constants work for intervals ending inside a step and are independent of Fourier support and higher Sobolev norms.

binders.type: smooth real mean-zero solution of the normalized KdV equation

record.statement: For T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0 there are C>0,tau0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that for every smooth real mean-zero datum u0 of H^gamma norm <=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, the fixed scheme and its Interp path satisfy sup_[0,T]||S_(-t)u(t)-V(t)||_2<=C*tau^gamma, hence max_(0<=n<=L)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. Constants are independent of every higher Sobolev norm and of spectral support.

There exist C>0 and tau0>0, depending only on T,gamma,R, such that for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(mathbbT) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R, the unique distributional solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma) obtained by smooth approximation and the fixed unfiltered iterates of Psi satisfy max_(0<=n<=L)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_L2<=C*tau^gamma for every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0. The constants are uniform over that entire datum ball and all these L; no Fourier-support restriction is imposed.
